candidate_causes.caveat: a readout that subtracts each odour's naive V is not a mechanism the fly has; it measures the direction of the learned change alone. Point 0 is undefined (V - V = 0)

estimate.metric: FLY-L right-direction share with the naive V removed (V(t) - V(0), same odours and seeds)

candidate_causes.cause: learned change too small: equilibrium between multiplicative depression and recovery r = 0.001 (observed tau ~15 battles, compartment_tau_fit)
candidate_causes.caveat: amp3.4 is a CRUDE bound, not a no-recovery estimate: 3.4 is the linear-regime deficit ratio, but the rule depresses multiplicatively, so without recovery edges would be driven unevenly toward the floor rather than the change scaled by 3.4. Both variants assume the change's direction is fixed and ignore the rule's tanh saturation and the changed choices / rewards. What new learning with another r would give is not estimated here

estimate.metric: FLY-L right-direction share at 120 with the learned change scaled

recovery.note: recover_pulse: after each DAN pulse every plastic edge moves r of the way back to w0 (plasticity.py). Odour key = (move type, opponent type set the brain saw: FLY-L the true one, FLY-OS the drawn one). no_recovery factor = r n / (1 - exp(-r n)), the linear-regime ratio of the deficit without recovery to the deficit with it for a constant depression per pulse - a crude figure: the rule is multiplicative, so without recovery edges would be driven unevenly toward the floor, not scaled. recovery_only_time_constant_battles = 1 / (r x pulses per battle) ignores depression; the observed approach (compartment_tau_fit) is faster

tau_fit.mechanism: plasticity.py depresses multiplicatively (w x (1 - lr tanh(.))) and recover_pulse moves r of the way back to w0: per pulse an edge approaches its equilibrium at rate (a + r), a = its depression rate, and the equilibrium deficit is a / (a + r). The observed tau is therefore shorter than the recovery-only 1 / (r x pulses per battle)
tau_fit.model: approach fraction (1 - w(t)) / (1 - w_eq) = 1 - exp(-t / tau), t = bin centre (battles), w_eq = mean of the 60-119 bins, w(0) = 1; least squares over a tau grid

weights_at_120.note: ratio w/w0; floor = share <= floor_tolerance = (0.2 + r 0.8)(1 + 1e-6): checkpoints are written after recover_pulse, so an edge held at the 0.2 floor reads 0.2008. floor_n is a LOWER BOUND: the 0.2008 bound catches an edge that touched the floor and then recovered exactly once; an edge that touched the floor and recovered twice reads 0.2016 (fly 25's min, 0.20160) and is not counted. The run's floor_contact (AC.3, <= 0.2 (1 + 1e-6)) cannot see such edges; at_w0 = unchanged (the rule depresses only and recovers toward w0, so w0 is the ceiling); confirm_active_kc = edges whose KC spiked for any confirmation-set FLY odour in the naive map

candidate_causes.method: checkpoint 120 vs w0 with the floor tolerance 0.2 + r 0.8 (weights_at_120.per_fly_floor_all_edges): at least a handful of edges per fly sit at the floor (a lower bound: 0.2008 catches one recovery after the floor only; fly 25's min 0.2016 is a floor edge recovered twice); the run's floor_contact (<= 0.2) could not see them

contrast_symmetry.argument: FLY-OS draws the opponent species for each side independently and uniformly from the same 16 (seed keys differ only by side), so the two sides' odours are exchangeable and d = X(side 0) - X(side 1) is symmetric about 0 for any fixed weights: P(d > 0) = (1 - P(d = 0)) / 2. FLY-L's d is fixed by the pair's two true odours and w0
